mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate comparative statements of the form 'A has N more (or fewer) items than B' into the equation A = B + N (or A = B - N) preserving the direction.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement explicitly says one person has more or fewer items than another.
mathgap.example: A statement like 'Taylor has 5 more oranges than Adolfo' should not be read as an absolute difference; it must be encoded as Taylor = Adolfo + 5.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: A direct count statement (e.g., 'A has N items') sets the current value of A to N at that point in the sequence, and later operations may modify it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a plain assignment of a quantity to a person.
mathgap.example: Reading 'Myles has 15 oranges' as setting Myles = 15, not as a permanent initial value.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the given order; apply each transfer, split, or redistribution immediately before interpreting later statements that refer to the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any transfer, conditional transfer, split, or redistribution clause.
mathgap.example: If 'Robert gives 3 oranges to Myles' appears before a comparison involving Myles, the comparison must use Myles' updated count.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate sentences equating two differences into the signed form (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'the number of X has more than Y is equal to the difference between the number of C and D'.
mathgap.example: The phrase 'X has more than Y is equal to the difference between C and D' becomes X - Y = C - D.

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction) – Correct Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement modifies a count by multiplication (e.g., 'X increases by N times'), treat it as a multiplicative scaling, not as addition or division.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a phrase like 'increases by N times' or 'decreases by N times' appears.
mathgap.example: For 'The number of apples that Sam has increases by 3 times', compute new = old × 3.

mathgap.title: Redistribute Equally Among Group
mathgap.principle: If a group of people redistributes their items so that each ends up with an equal amount, compute the average of the group's total and assign that to every member.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says two or more people 'redistribute' to ensure equal amounts.
mathgap.example: If Alice and Bob have 4 and 6 oranges and they redistribute equally, each ends with (4+6)/2 = 5.

mathgap.title: Comprehensive Constraint Extraction
mathgap.principle: Gather every constraint implied by each statement, even those that do not directly involve the queried person, to keep the full system of equations consistent.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For every statement in the problem, extract the algebraic relationship it imposes.
mathgap.example: A sentence about a transfer between two unrelated people still affects later constraints and must be recorded.

mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Treat both 'the number of X has more than Y' and 'the difference between the number of X and Y' as signed subtraction, preserving the order of names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a difference is mentioned, keep the sign according to the phrasing.
mathgap.example: 'The number of oranges that A has more than B' translates to A - B, not |A - B|.

mathgap.title: Difference Equality Numeric Evaluation
mathgap.principle: When a difference equality (A - B = C - D) involves variables whose values are already known, compute the numeric result directly and propagate it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After enough information is gathered to evaluate a difference equality numerically.
mathgap.example: If we know A=8, B=3, C=5, then D = A - B - C = 0.

mathgap.title: Fractional Increase Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret statements of the form 'the number of X increases by N/D times' as multiplying the current count by (1 + N/D), not by N/D alone.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a phrase uses a fractional multiplier after 'increases by' (e.g., '7/4 times').
mathgap.example: Wrong: treating 'The number of cucumbers that Austen has increases by 7/4 times' as new = old × 7/4. Correct: new = old × (1 + 7/4) = old × 11/4.

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes differences are always non‑negative and drops the order of the names.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate 'difference between X and Y' to the signed expression X - Y, preserving the given order.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model processes transfers as if they were simultaneous or later, ignoring temporal order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer, split, or redistribution immediately when the statement is encountered, updating counts before any later reference.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats an assignment as immutable, forgetting that later operations can modify the same variable.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Allow later transfers, splits, or multiplicative updates to overwrite the current value of a person.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term (including assuming positivity).
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model simplifies (A - B) = C - D to A = B + C, discarding D and any sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Keep the full equation (A - B) = (C - D) and solve for the unknowns while preserving both sides.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increases by N times' (including fractional N) as addition, division, or incorrect multiplication factor (e.g., using N/D instead of 1+N/D).
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses the phrase with simple scaling or additive increase, especially when a fraction is involved.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: For integer N, treat 'increases by N times' as multiplication by (1 + N). For a fraction N/D, multiply by (1 + N/D).
